objective: forward a bounded native Vulkan image, memory binding, and image-view lifecycle through the glibc-to-Bionic bridge without transmitting pointers or fabricating Vulkan handles

wire.representation: canonical fixed-width little-endian scalars and typed 64-bit bridge object IDs only
wire.native_reconstruction: the Bionic service resolves same-device native handles and reconstructs local VkImageCreateInfo, VkImageFormatListCreateInfo, VkImageStencilUsageCreateInfo, and VkImageViewCreateInfo records

supported_shape.images: bounded core 1D, 2D, or 3D non-sparse images with exclusive or bounded concurrent sharing
supported_shape.views: bounded core image views whose mip, layer, type, format mutability, and same-device image lineage are validated before native creation

ownership.image: typed BVB_OBJECT_IMAGE backed by a real native VkImage and parented to its VkDevice
ownership.image_view: typed BVB_OBJECT_IMAGE_VIEW backed by a real native VkImageView and parented to its image
ownership.bind: image and VkDeviceMemory must share the same device parent
ownership.explicit_destroy: view destruction removes and destroys the native view; image destruction refuses while a child view is live
ownership.device_teardown: remaining image views are destroyed before their images and before the native device

fail_closed: unknown, duplicate, overlong, or unsupported pNext records
over-limit queue-family or view-format arrays and malformed pointers
unsupported sparse, DRM-modifier, external-memory, compression, swapchain, or image-view extension shapes
invalid image dimensions, type relationships, samples, usages, layouts, flags, view ranges, or component/aspect enums
wrong-type, missing, cross-device, or wrong-parent object IDs
nonzero reserved or unused fixed-wire fields

dispatch_policy.promotion: exactly six image and image-view names move from required_unimplemented to executable

verification.canonical_codec: round trips all fixed records and rejects reserved-byte, over-limit, unsupported-chain, and wrong-type corruption
verification.cross_process_fake_driver: observed the exact native image and view create shapes, returned real non-dummy handles, returned 16384-byte memory requirements, bound real image memory, and aborted device destruction if service teardown leaked an image or view

first_remaining_call_in_dxvk_image_path.derivation: pinned DXVK createImageResource calls vkCreateImage at src/dxvk/dxvk_memory.cpp:1111 and immediately calls vkGetImageMemoryRequirements2 at line 1130 with VkMemoryDedicatedRequirements; E063 intentionally exposes only the requested legacy requirements entry
first_remaining_call_in_dxvk_image_path.consequence: the v2 requirements query and its dedicated-allocation pNext response must be implemented before this image allocation path can reach memory allocation and vkBindImageMemory

remaining: vkGetImageMemoryRequirements2 and its bounded VkMemoryDedicatedRequirements response
the existing ordinary allocation path rejects allocations above 16 MiB, smaller than a native-resolution RGBA image
additional image pNext shapes, sparse resources, buffer views, rendering commands, and virtual presentation remain separate gates
real private-Turnip execution, Tomb Raider output, and FPS remain unproven
reuse: Required deja searches returned no indexed prior image-resource implementation. Reused E034/E058 generated resolver-policy promotion, E046 fixed-width typed-object ownership, E056 local pNext reconstruction, and the existing buffer/device-memory lifecycle pattern.
